description: Huary Perry "U. P. " Wilson (September 4, 1934 – September 22, 2004) was an American electric blues guitarist and singer who performed Texas blues.

name: Johnny Winter

albums.name: The History of Rock, Volume Twenty Five (1984)

description: John Dawson Winter III (February 23, 1944 – July 16, 2014) was an American singer, guitarist, songwriter, and record producer.  Winter was known for his high-energy blues rock albums, live performances, and slide guitar playing from the late 1960s into the early 2000s.  He also produced three Grammy Award–winning albums for blues singer and guitarist Muddy Waters.

name: Jimmy Witherspoon
description: James Witherspoon (August 8, 1920 – September 18, 1997) was an American jump blues and jazz singer.

name: Big John Wrencher
description: Big John Wrencher (February 12, 1923 – July 15, 1977), also known as One Arm John, was an American blues harmonica player and singer, well known for playing at the Maxwell Street Market in Chicago in the 1960s.  He toured Europe in the 1970s.

name: Laith Al-Saadi
description:
Laith Al-Saadi (born October 5, 1977) is an American blues musician from Ann Arbor, Michigan. 
Al-Saadi gained nationwide recognition after he won a spot in the 2016 finale of the musical competition series The Voice.

name: Marcia Ball
description:
Marcia Ball (born March 20, 1949) is an American retired blues singer and pianist raised in Vinton, Louisiana. 
Ball was described in USA Today as "a sensation, saucy singer and superb pianist...  where Texas stomp-rock and Louisiana blues-swamp meet.

name: Chico Banks
description: Chico Banks (March 7, 1962 – December 3, 2008) was an American Chicago blues guitarist and singer.  He released one album, in 1997 on Evidence Music, produced by Larry Hoffman.  Banks was both a band leader and sideman, having played with Chicago's blues musicians from his late teens until his death at the age of 46.

name: L.V. Banks
description: L. V.  Banks (October 28, 1932 – May 2, 2011) was an American Chicago blues and soul blues guitarist, singer and songwriter.

name: Barrelhouse Chuck
description:
Barrelhouse Chuck (born Harvey Charles Goering; July 10, 1958 – December 12, 2016) was an American Chicago blues and electric blues pianist, keyboardist, singer, and songwriter. 
He claimed to be the only Chicago blues pianist to have studied under Sunnyland Slim, Pinetop Perkins, Blind John Davis, Detroit Junior, and Little Brother Montgomery.   His work appeared on sixteen albums.

name: Tab Benoit

albums.name: Legacy: The Best Of Tab Benoit (2012)

description:
Tab Benoit (born November 17, 1967) is an American blues guitarist, musician, and singer.  His playing combines a number of blues styles, primarily Delta blues. 
He plays a stock 1972 Fender Telecaster Thinline electric guitar and writes his own musical compositions.

name: Lurrie Bell
description: Lurrie Bell (born Lurrie C.  Bell, December 13, 1958, Chicago, Illinois, United States) is an American blues guitarist and singer.  His father was renowned blues harmonica player Carey Bell.

name: Cedric Burnside
description: Cedric O.  Burnside (born August 26, 1978) is an American electric blues guitarist, drummer, singer and songwriter.  He is the son of blues drummer Calvin Jackson and  grandson of blues singer, songwriter, and guitarist R.

name: Karen Carroll
description:
Karen Lynn Carroll (January 30, 1958 – March 9, 2016) was an American blues singer.  She was born to Mack Carroll and Alberta Simmons Carroll (stage name Jeanne Carroll). 
Her godparents were the jazz guitarist George Freeman and the blues vocalist Bonnie Lee.

name: Deborah Coleman
description: Deborah Coleman (October 3, 1956 – April 12, 2018) was an American blues musician.  Coleman won the Orville Gibson Award for "Best Blues Guitarist, Female" in 2001, and was nominated for a W. C.

name: Robert Cray

albums.name: 20th Century Masters: The Millennium Collection: The Best of Robert Cray (2002)

description: Robert William Cray (born August 1, 1953) is an American blues guitarist and singer.  He has led his own band and won five Grammy Awards.

name: Debbie Davies
description:
Debbie Davies (born August 22, 1952) is an American blues guitarist. 
Davies was born in Los Angeles, California, United States.  She has been the featured guitarist in several female based bands including Maggie Mayall and the Cadillacs (led by John Mayall's wife), and Fingers Taylor and the Ladyfinger Revue (who opened for Jimmy Buffett during his 1991 tour).

name: Boo Boo Davis
description: James "Boo Boo" Davis (born November 4, 1943) is an American electric blues musician.  Davis is one of the few remaining blues musicians who gained experience singing the blues in the Mississippi Delta, having sung to help pass the time while picking the cotton fields.

name: Ronnie Earl

albums.name: Heart and Soul The Best of Ronnie Earl (2006)

description:
Ronnie Earl (born Ronald Horvath, March 10, 1953, Queens, New York, United States) is an American blues guitarist and music instructor. 
Earl who grew up collecting various music records, pursued a degree in special education and education at Boston University.  He became interested in guitar after attending a Muddy Waters concert and began playing in the Boston blues scene.

name: Tinsley Ellis
description: Tinsley Ellis (born June 4, 1957) is an American blues and rock musician, who was born in Atlanta, Georgia, United States, and grew up in South Florida.   According to Billboard, "nobody has released more consistently excellent blues albums than Atlanta's Tinsley Ellis.  He sings like a man possessed and wields a mean lead guitar.

name: Sue Foley
description: Sue Foley (born March 29, 1968) is a Canadian multi-award-winning blues guitarist and singer/songwriter known for her fiery Texas blues style and refined acoustic touch.  A five-time Blues Music Award winner for Traditional Blues Female,   and a Juno recipient, she has shared the stage with musicians including B. B.

name: Robben Ford
description: Robben Lee Ford (born December 16, 1951) is an American blues, jazz, and rock guitarist.  He was a member of the L. A.

name: Anson Funderburgh
description: Anson Funderburgh (born James Anson Funderburgh; November 14, 1954) is an American blues guitar player and bandleader of Anson Funderburgh and the Rockets since 1978.  The band's style incorporates both Chicago blues and Texas blues.

name: Grady Gaines
description: Grady Gaines (May 14, 1934 – January 29, 2021) was an American electric blues, Texas blues and jazz blues tenor saxophonist, who performed and recorded with Little Richard in the 1950s.  He backed other musicians such as Dee Clark, Little Willie John, Sam Cooke, James Brown, Jackie Wilson, and Joe Tex.  He released three albums.

name: Terry Garland
description: Terry Ray Garland (June 3, 1953 – September 19, 2021), who was born in Johnson City, Tennessee, was an American blues guitarist, songwriter and singer.  The Allmusic journalist Niles J.  Frantz wrote that Garland was "a country blues interpreter who plays a National steel guitar, often with a slide, in the style of Bukka White and Fred McDowell.

name: Otis Grand
description: Fred Bishti (February 14, 1950 – June 2023), known professionally as Otis Grand, was a Lebanese-born American blues musician, best known for his album, Perfume & Grime (1996) and his exciting live performances.  He was honoured with the Presidential Medal for Arts by the Republic of Lebanon in 2009.

name: Guitar Slim Jr.
description: Guitar Slim Jr.  (born Rodney Glenn Armstrong, August 24, 1952, New Orleans, Louisiana, United States) is an American New Orleans blues guitarist and singer.  Over his lengthy playing career, he has worked with numerous other blues musicians.

name: Sandra Hall

albums.name: Take the Bit Out of My Blues (1998)

description: Sandra L.  Hall (born September 5, 1951) is an American blues and soul blues singer and songwriter.  She has been billed as  Atlanta's "Empress of the Blues" Hall is an Honorary Member of the Atlanta Blues Society.

name: Ted Hawkins

albums.name: Love You Most of All: More Songs From Venice Beach (1998)
Essential Recordings: Cold and Bitter Tears (2009)

description: Ted Hawkins (October 28, 1936 – January 1, 1995) was an American singer-songwriter born in Biloxi, Mississippi.  He split his time between his adopted hometown of Venice Beach, California, where he was a mostly anonymous street performer, and Europe and Australia, where he and his songs were better known and well received in clubs and small concert halls.

name: Colin James
description: Colin James  (born Colin James Munn; August 17, 1964) is a Canadian blues rock singer and songwriter.  James has been very successful in Canada, having attained seven Gold-certified albums in Canada during his career, including four Platinum albums and two Double Platinum albums.

name: L.V. Johnson
description: L. V.  Johnson (December 25, 1946 – November 22, 1994) was an American Chicago blues and soul-blues guitarist, singer and songwriter.

name: Keb' Mo'

albums.name: Martin Scorsese Presents the Blues: Keb’ Mo’ (2003)
Room on the Porch for Everyone (2025)

description: Kevin Roosevelt Moore (born October 3, 1951), known as Keb' Mo', is an American blues musician.  He is a singer, guitarist and songwriter, living in Nashville, Tennessee.  He has been described as "a living link to the seminal Delta blues that travelled up the Mississippi River and across the expanse of America.

name: Little Jimmy King
description:
Emmanuel Lynn Gales (December 4, 1964 – July 19, 2002), known professionally as Little Jimmy King, was an American Memphis blues guitarist, singer and songwriter.  A left-handed guitarist who played the instrument upside down, he concocted his stage name in deference to his two musical heroes, Jimi Hendrix and Albert King. 
He is best known for his tracks "Win, Lose or Draw" and "Upside Down and Backwards".

name: Lady Bianca
description:
Lady Bianca (born August 8, 1953) is an American electric blues singer, songwriter and arranger.  Lady Bianca has worked as a session singer, depicted Billie Holiday on stage, and since 1995 released six solo albums, three of which were nominated for a Grammy Award. 
She is currently based in Oakland, California.

name: Bob Margolin
description: Bob Margolin (born May 9, 1949) is an American electric blues guitarist.   His nickname is Steady Rollin'.  In 2026 Margolin was inducted into the Blues Hall of Fame.

name: Larry McCray
description: Larry McCray (born April 5, 1960), is an American blues guitarist and singer from Magnolia, Arkansas.

name: Kenny Neal
description:
Kenny Neal (born October 14, 1957), is an American blues guitar player, singer, and band member.  
Neal was born in New Orleans, Louisiana, the son of Raful Neal, and he comes from a musical family.  He has often performed with his brothers in his band.

name: Lucky Peterson
description: Judge Kenneth "Lucky" Peterson (December 13, 1964 – May 17, 2020) was an American musician who played contemporary blues, fusing soul, R&B, gospel and rock and roll.  He was a vocalist, guitarist and keyboardist.  Music journalist Tony Russell, in his book The Blues - From Robert Johnson to Robert Cray has said, "he may be the only blues musician to have had national television exposure in short pants.

name: Gary Primich
description: Gary Primich (April 20, 1958 – September 23, 2007) was an American blues harmonica player, singer, guitarist and songwriter.  He is best known for his 1995 album, Mr.  Freeze.

name: Johnny Rawls
description: Johnny Rawls (born September 10, 1951) is an American soul blues singer, guitarist, arranger, songwriter, and record producer.  He was influenced by the deep soul and gospel music of the 1960s, as performed by O.  V.

name: Sherman Robertson
description: Sherman Robertson (October 27, 1948 – January 28, 2021) was an American blues guitarist and singer who has been described as "one part zydeco, one part swamp blues, one part electric blues and one part classic rhythm and blues.

name: Duke Robillard

albums.name: Best Of Rounder Records - Rockin' Guitar Blues (2009)
Duke’s Box, the Blues and More

description: Michael John "Duke" Robillard (born October 4, 1948) is an American guitarist and singer.  He founded the band Roomful of Blues and was a member of the Fabulous Thunderbirds.  Although he is known as a rock and blues guitarist, he also plays jazz and swing.

name: Saffire – The Uppity Blues Women
description: Saffire – The Uppity Blues Women was a three-woman blues musical ensemble in the Washington, D. C.  area.

name: Kenny Wayne Shepherd
description: Kenny Wayne Shepherd (born Kenneth Wayne Brobst; June 12, 1977) is an American guitarist.  He has released several studio albums and experienced significant commercial success as a blues rock artist.

name: Cootie Stark
description: Johnny Miller (December 27, 1927 – April 14, 2005), known as Cootie Stark, was an American Piedmont blues guitarist, singer, and songwriter.  His best remembered recordings were "Metal Bottoms" and "Sandyland. " Stark was known as the "King of the Piedmont Blues.

name: Angela Strehli
description: Angela Strehli (born November 22, 1945) is an American electric blues singer and songwriter.  She is also a Texas blues historian and impresario.  Despite a sporadic recording career, Strehli spends time each year performing in Europe, the US and Canada.

name: Demetria Taylor
description: Demetria M.  Taylor (born February 28, 1973) is an American Chicago blues singer and songwriter.  Her father was Eddie Taylor, a fellow Chicago blues musician.

name: Melvin Taylor
description: Melvin Taylor (born March 13, 1959) is an American electric blues guitarist, based in Chicago.

name: Susan Tedeschi

albums.name: The Best of Susan Tedeschi: Episode One (2005)
The Best of Susan Tedeschi: Episode Two (2007)

description: Susan Tedeschi (; born November 9, 1970) is an American singer and guitarist.  A multiple Grammy Award nominee, she is a member of the Tedeschi Trucks Band, a conglomeration of her band, her husband Derek Trucks' band, and other musicians.

name: Maurice John Vaughn
description: Maurice John Vaughn (born May 10, 1952) is an American blues musician from Chicago, Illinois, United States.  He is a guitarist, saxophonist, keyboardist and singer.

name: Joe Louis Walker

albums.name: The Best of the Stony Plain Years (2014)

description: Louis Joseph Walker Jr.  (December 25, 1949 – April 30, 2025), known as Joe Louis Walker, was an American musician, best known as an electric blues guitarist, singer, songwriter and producer.  His knowledge of blues history is revealed by his use of older material and playing styles.

name: Carl Weathersby
description: Carlton Weathersby (February 24, 1953 – August 9, 2024) was an American electric blues vocalist, guitarist, and songwriter.  He worked with Albert King and Billy Branch, among others, and had a career as a solo artist.  He was nominated for the W.

name: Valerie Wellington
description: Valerie Wellington (November 14, 1959 – January 2, 1993) was an American singer who, in her short career, switched from singing opera to singing Chicago blues and electric blues.  On her 1984 album, Million Dollar Secret, she worked with Sunnyland Slim, Billy Branch, and Magic Slim.  She also worked with Lee "Shot" Williams.

name: Lil' Ed Williams
description: Lil' Ed Williams (born April 8, 1955, Chicago, Illinois) is an American blues slide guitarist, singer and songwriter.  With his backing band, the Blues Imperials, he has built up a loyal following.

name: Zora Young
description:
Zora Young (born January 21, 1948, West Point, Mississippi, United States) is an American blues singer.  She is distantly related to Howlin' Wolf. 
Young's family moved to Chicago when she was seven.

name: Ed Bell

albums.name: Complete Recorded Works in Chronological Order: 1927 - 1930 (1992)

description: Ed Bell (born 1905) was an American country blues guitarist and singer. Active in the late 1920s and early 1930s, he recorded for Paramount Records and is known for songs like 'Mamie Ley' and 'Old Country Stomp'.

name: Willie Brown

albums.name: Son House and the Great Delta Blues Singers (1928-1930) (1990)

description: Willie Lee Brown (1899 or August 6, 1900 – December 30, 1952) was an American blues guitar player and vocalist.  He performed and recorded with other blues musicians, including Son House and Charlie Patton, and influenced Robert Johnson and Muddy Waters.  Brown is considered one of the pioneering musicians of the Delta blues genre.

name: Tom Delaney
description: Tom Delaney (c. 1889 – c. 1963) was an American classic female blues songwriter and singer. He wrote several popular blues songs in the 1920s including 'Down Home Blues' and 'Terrible Blues', which were recorded by Bessie Smith and other blues singers of the era.

name: Richard "Hacksaw" Harney
description: Richard "Hacksaw" Harney (July 16, 1902 – December 25, 1973) was an American Delta blues guitarist and pianist.  He first entered a recording studio with his brother Maylon in 1928, to wax guitar work backing for separate tracks by Pearl Dickson and Walter Rhodes.  However,  Harney recorded rarely, until his belated solo album, Sweet Man (1972).

name: Katherine Henderson
description: Katherine Henderson (born c. 1898) was an American classic female blues singer. She recorded in the 1920s and was part of the classic female blues era.

albums.name: Complete Recorded Works in Chronological Order, Volume 2: 28 August 1928 to February 1930 (1992)
Complete Recorded Works in Chronological Order, Volume 1: 10 October 1927 to 27 August 1928 (1992)

description: Jim Jackson (c. 1890 – c. 1948) was an American country blues singer and guitarist. His 1927 recording of 'Jim Jackson's Kansas City Blues' was a hit and became one of the most recorded blues songs of the era.

The Originator Of Modern Guitar Blues (1980)

A pioneering figure in blues and jazz guitar, he recorded extensively from the 1920s through the 1960s and influenced countless guitarists with his sophisticated single-string solo style.

name: Mary Johnson

albums.name: Complete Recorded Works In Chronological Order 1929-1936

description: Mary Johnson (c. 1903 – c. 1970) was an American classic female blues singer. She recorded in the late 1920s and 1930s, often accompanied by top jazz and blues musicians of the period.

albums.name: Complete Recorded Works in Chronological Order, Vol. 1: 1935-1939 (1990)
Complete Recorded Works in Chronological Order, Volume 2: 1939-1943

description: Clarence Lofton (March 28, 1887, 1896 or 1897 – January 9, 1957), credited as Cripple Clarence Lofton, was an American boogie-woogie pianist and singer born in Tennessee.

name: Charlie "Specks" McFadden

albums.name: Complete Recorded Works In Chronological Order 1929-1937 (1993)

description: Charles Pertum, known professionally as Charlie "Specks" McFadden (April 24, 1895 – November 15, 1966), was an American country blues singer and songwriter.  On his few recordings, released from 1929 to 1937, he was accompanied by Roosevelt Sykes, Lonnie Johnson, Pinetop Sparks and others.  His most notable song was one he wrote, "Groceries on the Shelf (Piggly Wiggly)", which he recorded in Grafton, Wisconsin, about February 1930.

name: Jay McShann

albums.name: The Band That Jumps The Blues! (1973)
Last of the Whorehouse Piano Players -- The Original Sessions (1992)

description: James Columbus "Jay" McShann (January 12, 1916 – December 7, 2006) was an American jazz pianist, vocalist, composer, and bandleader.  He led bands in Kansas City, Missouri, that included Charlie Parker, Bernard Anderson, Walter Brown, and Ben Webster.

name: Whistlin' Alex Moore

albums.name: Complete Recorded Works 1929-1951 In Chronological Order (1993)
From North Dallas To The East Side (1994)

description: Alexander Herman "Whistlin' Alex" Moore (November 22, 1899 – January 20, 1989), was an American blues pianist, singer and whistler.  He is best remembered for his recordings of "Blue Bloomer Blues" (which he first recorded in 1929, as well as later in life), "Across the Atlantic Ocean" and "Black Eyed Peas and Hog Jowls".

name: Piano Red

albums.name: Piano Red a.k.a. Dr. Feelgood: The Doctor's In! (1993)
The Blues Collection: Piano Red, Live and Feelin' Good (1996)
Piano Red aka Dr. Feelgood: Rocks (2008)

description: Willie Lee Perryman (October 19, 1911 – July 25, 1985), usually known professionally as Piano Red and later in life as Dr.  Feelgood, was an American blues musician, the first to hit the pop music charts.  He was a self-taught pianist who played in the barrelhouse blues style (a loud percussive type of blues piano suitable for noisy bars or taverns).

name: Red Nelson
description: Red Nelson (born c. 1907) was an American country blues singer. He recorded in the 1930s and was known for his distinctive vocal style.

name: Walter Roland

albums.name: Complete Recorded Works in Chronological Order, Volume 2: 1934-1935
Complete Recorded Works in Chronological Order, Volume 1: 1933

description: Walter Roland (possibly December 20, 1902 – October 12, 1972) was an American blues and boogie-woogie pianist, guitarist and singer, noted for his association with Lucille Bogan, Josh White and Sonny Scott.  The music journalist Gérard Herzhaft stated that Roland was "a great piano player...  as comfortable in boogie-woogies as in slow blues," adding that "Roland – with his manner of playing and his singing – was direct and rural.

name: Henry "Son" Sims
description: Henry "Son" Sims (August 22, 1890 – December 23, 1958) was an American Delta blues fiddler and songwriter.  He is best known as an accompanist for Charley Patton and the young Muddy Waters.

name: J. T. "Funny Papa" Smith
description: J. T. 'Funny Papa' Smith (c. 1899 – c. 1940) was an American country blues singer. He recorded in the early 1930s and was known for his humorous songs.

name: Pinetop Sparks
description: Aaron "Pinetop" Sparks (born Aaron Gant, May 22, 1910 – November 5, 1935) was an American blues pianist active in St.  Louis in the early 1930s.  He and his brother, Milton “Lindberg” Sparks (born Marion Gant), recorded songs from between 1932 and 1935.

name: Speckled Red

albums.name: Complete Recorded Works 1929-1938 in Chronological Order (1993)

description: Rufus George Perryman (October 23, 1892 – January 2, 1973), known as Speckled Red, was an American blues and boogie-woogie piano player and singer noted for his recordings of "The Dirty Dozens", exchanges of insults and vulgar remarks that have long been a part of African-American folklore.

name: Frank Stokes

albums.name: The Blues Collection: Furry Lewis & Frank Stokes, Beale Street Blues (1995)
The Victor Recordings in Chronological Order (1928-1929) (2000)
The Best Of Frank Stokes - Classic Recordings of the 1920s (2005)

description: Frank Stokes (January 1, 1888 – September 12, 1955) was an American blues guitarist, singer, and songwriter. A key figure in the development of the Memphis blues style, he recorded both as a solo artist and as part of the Beale Street Sheiks.

name: Johnny Temple

albums.name: Complete Recorded Works In Chronological Order, Volume 2 (17 October 1938 To 4 April 1940) (1994)
Complete Recorded Works In Chronological Order, Volume 3: 1940-1949 (1994)
Complete Recorded Works in Chronological Order, Volume 1: 14 May 1935 to 22 April 1938 (1994)

description: Johnny Temple (August 8, 1927 – January 9, 1994) was an American country blues singer and guitarist. He recorded for Decca Records in the 1930s and 1940s and was known for his distinctive vocal style and guitar work in the country blues tradition.

name: Henry Townsend
description: Henry Townsend (October 27, 1909 – September 23, 2006) was an American blues pianist, guitarist, and singer. With a career spanning eight decades, he was one of the last surviving links to the early blues era and continued performing into his 90s.

name: Sylvester Weaver

albums.name: Complete Recorded Works in Chronological Order, Vol. 2: 31 August to 30 November 1927 (1992)
Complete Recorded Works in Chronological Order, Volume 1: 1923-1927 (1992)

description: Sylvester Weaver (July 25, 1897 – April 4, 1960) was an American blues guitarist and singer. He was among the first blues guitarists to record, cutting tracks in 1923 that are considered milestones in the development of country blues.

name: Oscar "Buddy" Woods

albums.name: Texas Slide Guitars: Complete Recorded Works 1930-1938 in Chronological Order (1992)

description:
Oscar "Buddy" Woods (April 7, 1903 – December 14, 1955) was an American Texas blues guitarist, singer and songwriter. 
Woods, who was an early blues pioneer in lap steel, slide guitar playing, recorded thirty-five tracks between 1930 and 1940.  He recorded solo and as part of a duo, the Shreveport Home Wreckers, and with a six- or seven-piece group, the Wampus Cats.

name: Boogie Woogie Red
description: Boogie Woogie Red (October 18, 1925 – July 2, 1992) was an American Detroit blues, boogie-woogie and jazz pianist, singer and songwriter.  At different times he worked with Sonny Boy Williamson I, Washboard Willie, Baby Boy Warren, Lonnie Johnson, Tampa Red, John Lee Hooker and Memphis Slim.

name: Clarence "Gatemouth" Brown
description: Clarence "Gatemouth" Brown (April 18, 1924 – September 10, 2005) was an American singer and multi-instrumentalist from Louisiana.  He was best-known as a blues performer, but his music was often eclectic and also touched on genres including country, jazz and rock and roll.  Brown won a Grammy Award for Best Traditional Blues Album in 1983 for his album, Alright Again!

name: Walter Brown

albums.name: Blues & Rhythm Series: The Chronological Walter Brown 1945-1947 (2001)
Blues & Rhythm Series: The Chronological Walter Brown 1947-1951 (2002)

description: Walter Brown (August 31, 1919 – May 25, 1956) was an American R&B and blues singer. He recorded with Jay McShann's orchestra and had hits with 'Don't You Want a Man Like Me' and 'Confessin' the Blues'.

name: George "Mojo" Buford
description: George Carter "Mojo" Buford Jr.   (November 10, 1929 – October 11, 2011), was an American blues harmonica player best known for his work in Muddy Waters's band.

name: Eddie "Guitar" Burns
description: Eddie "Guitar" Burns (February 8, 1928 – December 12, 2012) was an American Detroit blues guitarist, harmonica player, and singer and songwriter.  Among Detroit bluesmen, Burns was deemed to have been exceeded in stature by only John Lee Hooker.

name: Arthur "Big Boy" Crudup

albums.name: Charly Blues Masterworks Volume 50: Mean Ol' Frisco (1993)
Complete Recorded Works 1941-1956 in Chronological Order, Volume 2: 6 September 1946 to 11 March 1949 (1993)

description: Arthur William "Big Boy" Crudup (August 24, 1905 – March 28, 1974) was an American Delta blues singer, songwriter and guitarist.  He is best known, outside blues circles, for his songs "That's All Right" (1946), "My Baby Left Me" and "So Glad You're Mine", later recorded by Elvis Presley and other artists.

name: James Crutchfield
description: James Crutchfield (May 25, 1912 – December 7, 2001) was a St.  Louis barrelhouse blues singer, piano player and songwriter whose career spanned seven decades.  His repertoire consisted of original and classic blues and boogie-woogie and Depression-era popular songs.

name: James "Thunderbird" Davis
description: James Louis Huston, better known as James "Thunderbird" Davis (November 10, 1938 – January 24, 1992), was an American Texas blues and electric blues guitarist, singer and songwriter.  He recorded several singles for Duke Records in the early 1960s, achieving moderate success with "Blue Monday" (1963).  He dropped out of public attention until his career was revived in 1989 with the release of his album Check Out Time.

name: David "Honeyboy" Edwards
description: David "Honeyboy" Edwards (June 28, 1915 – August 29, 2011) was an American delta blues guitarist and singer from Mississippi.

name: Robert "Big Mojo" Elem
description: Robert "Big Mojo" Elem (January 22, 1928 – February 5, 1997) was an American Chicago blues bass guitarist and singer.  Although he recorded only one studio album in his long career, Elem was a part of the Chicago blues scene for over 40 years.  He variously backed Arthur "Big Boy" Spires, Lester Davenport, Freddie King, Magic Sam, Junior Wells, Shakey Jake Harris, Jimmy Dawkins, Luther Allison, and Otis Rush.

name: Johnny Fuller

albums.name: West Coast R&B - Blues Legend - Vol.2
West Coast R&B - Blues Legend - Vol.1

description: Johnny Fuller (April 29, 1929 – May 20, 1985) was an American West Coast blues guitarist, pianist and singer. He recorded for various labels in the 1950s and 1960s and is best known for his songs 'The Lone Wolf' and 'Tragic Love'.

name: Henry Gray

albums.name: The Henry Gray & Bob Corritore Sessions - Vol. 1 - Blues Won't Let Me Take My Rest (2015)

description: Henry Gray (January 19, 1925 – February 17, 2020) was an American Louisiana blues pianist and singer. He is best known for his work with Howlin' Wolf in the 1950s and for his long career playing swamp blues in Louisiana.

name: Peter Green
description: Peter Green (born Peter Allen Greenbaum, October 29, 1946) is an English blues rock singer-songwriter and guitarist. He founded Fleetwood Mac and is known for his distinctive guitar playing and songs like 'Black Magic Woman' and 'Albatross'.

name: Luther "Guitar Junior" Johnson

albums.name: Charly Blues Masterworks, Volume 1: The Crawl (1993)

description: Luther "Guitar Junior" Johnson (April 11, 1939 – December 25, 2022) was an American blues singer and guitarist.

name: Luther "Georgia Boy" Johnson

albums.name: They Call Me the Popcorn Man (2002)

description: Lucious Brinson Johnson (August 30, 1934 – March 18, 1976), known as Luther "Georgia Boy" Johnson, was an American Chicago blues and electric blues guitarist, singer and songwriter.  AllMusic journalist Ron Wynn stated, "Johnson's own inimitable vocals, raspy lines and tart guitar eventually create his own aura...   a good, occasionally outstanding blues artist.

name: Eddie King
description: Eddie King (April 21, 1938 – March 14, 2012) was an American Chicago blues guitarist, singer and songwriter. A protégé of Slim Harpo, King recorded for several labels and worked with Freddie King and other Chicago blues legends.

name: Bob Kirkpatrick
description: Bob Kirkpatrick (born January 10, 1934) is an American Texas blues guitarist, singer and songwriter. Known for his classy, jazzy guitar style, he recorded the album 'Going Back to Texas' in 1996 and has worked with many blues musicians in the Texas scene.

name: Luke "Long Gone" Miles
description: Luke "Long Gone" Miles (May 8, 1925 – November 22, 1987) was an American Texas blues and electric blues singer and songwriter.  He was a protégé of Lightnin' Hopkins and variously recorded or performed with Hopkins, Sonny Terry, Brownie McGhee and Willie Chambers.  Miles is best known for his 1964 album Country Born, issued by World Pacific Records.

name: Matt "Guitar" Murphy

albums.name: In Session: From Memphis to Chicago 1952-1961 (2020)

description: Matthew Tyler Murphy (December 29, 1929 – June 15, 2018), known as Matt "Guitar" Murphy, was an American blues guitarist and singer-songwriter.  He was associated with Memphis Slim, The Blues Brothers and Howlin' Wolf.  In 2012, Murphy was elected to the Blues Hall of Fame.

name: Dan Pickett
description: Dan Pickett (born James Fuchs, October 27, 1919 – January 18, 1974) was an American country blues guitarist and singer. He recorded in the late 1940s and his work was later released on compilation albums, showcasing his East Coast Piedmont blues style.

name: Bobby Rush

albums.name: Chicken Heads: A 50‐Year History of Bobby Rush (2015)

description: Bobby Rush (born Emmett Ellis Jr., November 23, 1946) is an American blues and R&B musician, singer and songwriter. A veteran of the chitlin' circuit, Rush is known for his energetic stage shows and hits like 'Chicken Heads' and 'Sue'. He has been recording for over 50 years and won a Grammy Award in 2017.

name: George "Harmonica" Smith

albums.name: Now You Can Talk About Me (1998)
Now You Can Talk About Me (1998)

description: George "Harmonica" Smith (born Allen George Smith, April 22, 1924 – October 2, 1983) was an American electric blues harmonica player.  Apart from his solo recordings, Smith is best known for his work backing both Muddy Waters and Big Mama Thornton.

name: Moses "Whispering" Smith
description: Moses "Whispering" Smith (January 25, 1932 – April 28, 1984) was an American blues harmonicist and singer.  He recorded tracks including "A Thousand Miles from Nowhere" and "Texas Flood" and worked with Lightnin' Slim and with Silas Hogan.  He was inducted into the Louisiana Blues Hall of Fame.

name: Otis "Big Smokey" Smothers
description: Otis "Big Smokey" Smothers (March 21, 1929 – July 23, 1993) was an American Chicago blues guitarist and singer.  He was a member of Howlin' Wolf's backing band and worked with Muddy Waters, Jimmy Rogers, Bo Diddley, Ike Turner, J.  T.

name: Arthur "Big Boy" Spires
description: Arthur "Big Boy" Spires (February 25, 1912 – October 22, 1990) was an American blues singer and guitarist who recorded for several record labels in Chicago in the 1950s and 1960s.

name: Taj Mahal

albums.name: The Best of Taj Mahal, Volume 1 (1981)

description: Taj Mahal (born Henry St. Claire Fredericks, May 17, 1942) is an American blues musician. A multi-instrumentalist who plays guitar, piano, and banjo, he has been a leading figure in blues and world music since the 1960s, known for incorporating diverse musical influences into his blues foundation.

name: Baby Tate
description: Baby Tate (born Bessie Mae Tate, January 28, 1919 – August 21, 1974) was an American Piedmont blues singer and guitarist. She performed and recorded in the 1960s folk blues revival, showcasing traditional country blues style.

name: Sam Taylor

albums.name: サム・テイラー全集～魅惑のテナー・サックス (2008)

description: Sam Taylor (October 9, 1916 – February 2, 1990) was an American blues and R&B tenor saxophonist and singer. A session musician in Houston and New York, he played on numerous hit records including Ray Charles' 'What'd I Say' and worked with many major blues and R&B artists.

name: Johnny "Big Moose" Walker
description:
Johnny "Big Moose" Walker (June 27, 1927 –  November 27, 1999) was an American Chicago blues and electric blues pianist and organist.  He worked with many blues musicians, including Ike Turner, Sonny Boy Williamson II, Lowell Fulson, Choker Campbell, Elmore James, Earl Hooker, Muddy Waters, Otis Spann, Sunnyland Slim, Jimmy Dawkins and Son Seals. 
Walker was primarily a piano player but was also proficient on the electronic organ and the bass guitar (he played the bass guitar when backing Muddy Waters).

name: Golden "Big" Wheeler
description: Golden "Big" Wheeler (December 15, 1929 – July 20, 1998) was an American Chicago blues and electric blues singer, harmonicist and songwriter.  He released two albums in his lifetime and is best known for his recordings of the songs "Damn Good Mojo" and "Bone Orchard".  He worked with the Ice Cream Men and Jimmy Johnson.

name: Lester Williams

albums.name: I Can’t Lose With the Stuff I Use (1993)

description: Lester Williams (October 5, 1919 – December 12, 1990) was an American Texas blues guitarist and singer. He recorded for several labels in the 1950s and is best known for his song 'I Can't Lose With the Stuff I Use'.

name: Alan Wilson
description: Alan Wilson (July 4, 1943 – September 3, 1970), known as 'The Blind Owl', was an American musician, best known as the co-founder, lead guitarist, and co-lead singer of the blues-rock band Canned Heat. His distinctive high voice and slide guitar playing were key elements of the band's sound.

name: Billy Wright

albums.name: Blues & Rhythm Series: The Chronological Billy Wright 1949-1951 (2002)

description: Billy Wright (May 21, 1918 – October 28, 1991) was an American R&B and blues singer. A flamboyant performer known as the 'Prince of the Blues,' Wright was a significant influence on Little Richard and recorded for several record labels in the 1940s and 1950s.

name: Johnny "Man" Young
description: Johnny "Man" Young (January 1, 1917 – April 18, 1974) was an American blues singer, mandolin player, and guitarist, significant as one of the first of the new generation of electric blues artists to record in Chicago after the Second World War.  He was one of the few mandolin players active in blues music in the postwar era.  His nickname, Man, came from his playing the mandolin.

name: Linsey Alexander
description: Linsey Alexander (July 23, 1942 – February 22, 2025) was an American blues songwriter, vocalist, and guitarist.  He was a fixture in clubs on Chicago's North Side for nearly two decades and played with numerous blues musicians, including Buddy Guy, A. C.

name: James Armstrong
description: James Armstrong (born November 3, 1961) is an American blues guitarist, singer and songwriter. Based in Detroit, Armstrong has released several albums and is known for his contemporary take on the Chicago blues tradition.

name: Dexter Allen
description:
Dexter Allen (born July 10, 1970) is an American blues musician, singer, songwriter and guitarist. 
Formerly the lead guitarist for the Airtight Band and blues musician Bobby Rush, he received a Jackson Music Award in 2008 for Male Vocalist of the Year.  That same year, he debuted his first album titled Bluezin My Way.

name: Terry "Harmonica" Bean
description:
Terry Wayne "Harmonica" Bean (born January 26, 1961) is an American blues harmonicist, guitarist and songwriter.  He has released seven albums since 2001, and appeared in three film documentaries charting present day blues experiences. 
Bean has dedicated himself to promoting older blues stylings, such as Delta blues and Hill country blues.

name: Chris Beard
description: Chris Beard (born February 18, 1973) is an American blues guitarist, singer and songwriter. The son of blues guitarist Joe Beard, Chris has continued the family tradition, releasing albums that blend traditional blues with contemporary elements.

name: Adolphus Bell
description: Adolphus Bell (June 5, 1944 – October 28, 2013) was an American electric blues musician, best known as a one-man band.  He performed in a professional capacity for five decades and released two albums on the Music Maker label.   He also played at various music festivals.

name: Eric Bibb

albums.name: A Collection of Cyndee Peters and Eric Bibb (1991)

description: Eric Charles Bibb (born August 16, 1951) is a Grammy-nominated American-born blues singer and songwriter.

name: Blind Mississippi Morris
description: Blind Mississippi Morris (born Morris Cummings; April 6, 1955 in Clarksdale, Mississippi, United States) is an American blues musician.

name: Skeeter Brandon
description:
Skeeter Brandon (April 22, 1948 – March 20, 2008) was an American blind blues keyboardist, singer and songwriter. 
From 1966 to 1991, Brandon played in various bands across the United States.  He joined Highway 61 in 1991, and recorded four albums in that ensemble until their break-up in 2001.

name: Ronnie Baker Brooks
description: Ronnie Baker Brooks (born January 23, 1967) is an American Chicago blues and soul blues guitarist, singer and songwriter.  He was a respected club performer in Chicago, even before recording three solo albums for Watchdog Records.   The son of fellow Chicago blues musician Lonnie Brooks, he is the brother of another blues guitarist, Wayne Baker Brooks.

name: Jimmy Burns
description: Jimmy Burns (born February 27, 1943) is an American soul blues and electric blues guitarist, singer and songwriter.  Although he was born in the Mississippi Delta, Burns has spent nearly all his life in Chicago.  His elder brother, Eddie "Guitar" Burns, was a Detroit blues musician.

name: William Clarke
description: William Clarke (July 21, 1951 – November 2, 1996) was an American blues harmonica player. A leading figure in the West Coast blues scene, Clarke was known for his powerful amplified harmonica playing and his work with the Hollywood Fats Band and as a solo artist.

name: Shemekia Copeland
description: Charon Shemekia Copeland (born April 10, 1979) is an American electric blues vocalist.  She has released 12 albums, won nine Blues Music Awards, and won five Blues Blast Music Awards.  In 2024, Copeland received nominations at the 67th Annual Grammy Awards for Best American Roots Performance, Best American Roots Song, and Best Contemporary Blues Album.

name: Guy Davis
description: Guy Davis (born May 12, 1952) is an American blues guitarist, singer, and songwriter. The son of actors Ossie Davis and Ruby Dee, Davis has carved out his own path in the blues world, specializing in traditional country blues and Piedmont styles.

name: Thornetta Davis
description: Thornetta Davis (born August 11, 1963) is an American Detroit blues and rhythm and blues singer.  She has opened for Bonnie Raitt, Gladys Knight, and Etta James, and sang backing vocals on Bob Seger's 1991 album, The Fire Inside.  She also worked with Kid Rock and Alberta Adams, and has released three solo albums.

name: Little Arthur Duncan
description: Little Arthur Duncan (February 5, 1934 – August 20, 2008) was an American Chicago blues and electric blues harmonica player, singer, and songwriter.  He was a member of the Backscratchers and over his career was associated with Earl Hooker, Twist Turner, Illinois Slim and Rick Kreher.

name: Kirk Fletcher
description: Kirk Fletcher (born December 23, 1975) is an American electric blues guitarist, singer, and songwriter. Known for his work with the Fabulous Thunderbirds and the Mannish Boys, Fletcher blends traditional blues with contemporary sensibilities and has backed artists like Joe Bonamassa.

name: Rick Franklin
description: Frederick "Rick" Franklin (born March 16, 1952) is an American Piedmont blues guitarist, singer and songwriter.  With various other musicians, Franklin has released four albums to date and works as a blues musicologist.

name: Larry Garner
description: Larry Garner (born July 8, 1952 in New Orleans, Louisiana, United States) is a Louisiana blues musician best known for his 1994 album Too Blues.

name: Larry Hamilton
description: Larry Hamilton (March 11, 1931 – July 20, 1996) was an American blues guitarist and singer. He recorded for several labels in the 1950s and 1960s and was part of the St. Louis blues scene.

name: Odessa Harris
description:
Dessie Mae Williams, known professionally as Odessa Harris (June 8, 1936 – August 18, 2007) was an American blues and jazz singer. 
In a lengthy career, Harris toured for two years with B. B.

name: Big Boy Henry
description: Richard Leslie Henry  (born May 26, 1921  – December 5, 2004), better known as Big Boy Henry, was an American Piedmont blues guitarist, singer and songwriter.  His most notable recording was  "Mr.  President", a protest against cuts in social welfare undertaken by President Ronald Reagan.

name: George Higgs
description: George Higgs (March 9, 1930 – January 29, 2013) was an American Piedmont blues acoustic guitarist, harmonicist, singer and songwriter.  He recorded three albums in his lifetime, although he spent over sixty years performing regularly, mainly in his home State.  In 1993, Higgs was granted the North Carolina Heritage Award from the North Carolina Arts Council.

name: Fruteland Jackson
description: Fruteland Jackson (born June 9, 1953) is an American electric blues guitarist, singer and songwriter.  Henry Townsend stated, "My respect for Fruteland Jackson is very high.  He and my boy Alvin Youngblood Hart is the future sound of true acoustic blues.

name: Johnny "Yard Dog" Jones
description: Johnny "Yard Dog" Jones (June 21, 1941 – September 15, 2015) was an American Chicago blues and soul blues singer, guitarist, harmonica player, and songwriter.  He won a W. C.

name: Paul "Wine" Jones
description: R. L. Burnside, Big Jack Johnson, Roosevelt "Booba" Barnes and James "Super Chikan" Johnson were "present-day exponents of an edgier, electrified version of the raw, uncut Delta blues sound"

name: Tutu Jones
description: Tutu Jones (born September 9, 1966) is an American electric blues and soul blues guitarist, singer and songwriter.  He has cited Freddie King and Z.  Z.

name: Harrison Kennedy
description: Harrison Kennedy (born April 24, 1945) is an American soul blues and R&B singer. Originally a member of the Detroit Emeralds, Kennedy has had a long solo career and is known for his powerful voice and blend of blues with soul and funk influences.

name: Chris Thomas King
description: Chris Thomas King (born Durwood Christopher Thomas, October 14, 1962) is an American blues musician and actor based in New Orleans, Louisiana.

name: Johnny Laws
description: Johnny Laws (January 12, 1943 – March 28, 2021) was an American Chicago blues guitarist, singer and songwriter.  A regular performer for over half a century in Chicago's South Side clubs, Laws released two albums, including Burnin' in My Soul, of which Blues & Rhythm magazine in November 1999 noted, "It's a real shame that Johnny Laws has been unjustly ignored in the past...  This is an enjoyable CD...

name: Professor Eddie Lusk
description: Eddie James Lusk, Jr.  known professionally as Professor Eddie Lusk (September 21, 1948 – August 26, 1992) was an American Chicago blues musician.  An ordained minister, Lusk carved out a successful career in the blues and variously worked with Luther Allison, Buddy Guy, Jimmy Johnson, Koko Taylor, Phil Guy, Jimmy Dawkins,  Sunnyland Slim, Michael Coleman, Fenton Robinson, Syl Johnson, and Otis Rush.

name: Johnnie Marshall
description: Johnnie B. Marshall Jr. (born June 2, 1961) is an American electric blues guitarist, songwriter, and singer. A contemporary blues artist, Marshall blends traditional blues with modern elements and has released several albums showcasing his guitar work and vocals.

name: Clara McDaniel
description: Clara McDaniel (born November 26, 1948) is an American blues singer and songwriter.  She released her debut album, Unwanted Child, in 1997 and has worked with notable blues musicians including Albert King, Tommy Bankhead, Bobby Bland, Little Milton, Oliver Sain, and Ike Turner.

name: Jay Owens
description: Jay Owens (born February 10, 1969) is an American blues guitarist, singer and songwriter. Known for his work in the Texas blues scene, Owens combines traditional blues with rock and soul influences.

name: Sista Monica Parker
description: Sista Monica Parker (April 27, 1956 – October 9, 2014) was an American electric blues and soul singer. Known for her powerful voice and gospel-inflected blues style, Parker recorded several albums and performed at major blues festivals before her untimely death.

name: Neal Pattman
description: Neal Pattman (January 10, 1926 – May 4, 2005) was an American electric blues harmonica player, singer and songwriter.  Sometimes billed as Big Daddy Pattman, he is best known for his self-penned tracks, "Prison Blues" and "Goin' Back To Georgia".   In the latter, and most notable stages of his long career, Pattman worked with Cootie Stark, Taj Mahal, Dave Peabody, Jimmy Rip, Kenny Wayne Shepherd, Guitar Gabriel, and Lee Konitz.

name: Asie Payton
description:
Asie Reed Payton (April 12, 1937 – May 19, 1997) was an American blues musician, who lived most of his life in Holly Ridge, Mississippi, in the Mississippi Delta.   Born in Washington County, Mississippi, he sang and played the guitar, but made his living as a farmer. 
Near the end of his life he recorded one album, Worried, for the Fat Possum Records label, which was released after his death.

name: Kelly Joe Phelps
description: Kelly Joe Phelps (October 5, 1959 – May 31, 2022) was an American musician and songwriter.  His music has been characterized as a mixture of delta blues and jazz.

name: Lonnie Pitchford
description:
Lonnie Pitchford (October 8, 1955 – November 8, 1998) was an American blues musician and instrument maker from Lexington, Mississippi, United States.   He was one of only a handful of young African American musicians from Mississippi who had learned and was continuing the Delta blues and country blues traditions of the older generations. 
In addition to the acoustic and electric guitar, Pitchford was skilled at the one-string guitar and diddley bow, a one-string instrument of African origin, as well as the double bass, piano and harmonica.

name: Gene "Birdlegg" Pittman
description: Eugene P.  Pittman  (born May 10, 1947), better known as  Gene "Birdlegg" Pittman, is an American blues harmonicist, singer and songwriter.  He was inspired by the harmonica playing and styling of Sonny Boy Williamson II and Sonny Terry, and started playing the harmonica in 1974, turning fully professional three years later.

name: Henry Qualls

albums.name: The Blues from the Deep South (1994)

description: Henry Qualls (July 8, 1934 – December 7, 2003) was an American Texas and country blues guitarist and singer.  He found success late in his life after being "discovered" in 1993 by the Dallas Blues Society.  He released his only album in 1994 but toured globally playing at a number of festivals.

name: Andy Rodgers

albums.name: American Songbook Series: Richard Rodgers & Lorenz Hart (1992)
The World’s Most Beautiful Melodies: The Sweetest Sounds / Great Songs of Richard Rodgers (1993)

description: Andy Rodgers (born October 18, 1983) is a Scottish blues singer known for his interpretations of blues standards and Broadway material. His performances blend traditional blues with theatrical elements.

name: Mighty Mo Rodgers
description:
Mighty Mo Rodgers (born July 24, 1942) is an American electric blues musician, singer, songwriter, and record producer, who has released eight albums to date.  He has been influenced by the work of Aretha Franklin, Bobby Bland, Eddie Boyd, Jimmy Reed, Otis Redding, Sam & Dave, and Willie Dixon. 
Bonnie Raitt noted that "Mo Rodgers' music is a breath of fresh air in the blues/R&B world.

name: Roy Rogers

albums.name: The Republic Years From the Original Soundtrack (1984)
Christmas With Roy Rogers and Dale Evans (1992)
The Country Music Hall of Fame: Roy Rogers (1992)

description:
Roy Rogers (born Leonard Franklin Slye; November 5, 1911 – July 6, 1998), nicknamed the King of the Cowboys, was an American singer, actor, television host, and rodeo performer. 
Following early work under his given name, first as co-founder of the Sons of the Pioneers and then as an actor, the rebranded Rogers became one of the most famous and popular Western stars of his era. 
He appeared in almost 90 motion pictures, as well as numerous episodes of his self-titled radio program that lasted nine years.

name: Isaac Scott
description: Isaac Scott (June 11, 1945 – November 16, 2001) was an American blues guitarist and singer. Based in the Pacific Northwest, Scott was known for his West Coast blues style and his work in the Seattle blues scene.

name: Lonnie Shields
description: Lonnie Shields (born April 17, 1956) is an American electric blues singer, songwriter, and guitarist.  His primary influence was B. B.

name: Eddie Taylor Jr.
description: Eddie Taylor Jr. (March 27, 1972 – March 8, 2019) was an American Chicago blues guitarist, singer and songwriter. The son of blues legend Eddie Taylor, he carried on his father's musical legacy, recording several albums for Wolf Records and performing in the Chicago blues tradition.

name: Otis Taylor
description: Otis Taylor (born July 30, 1948) is an American blues musician. A multi-instrumentalist and songwriter, Taylor is known for his storytelling through songs that often explore historical and social themes, blending traditional blues with folk and country influences.

name: Lil' Dave Thompson
description: David Lonzo Thompson (May 21, 1969 – February 14, 2010) was an American electric blues guitarist, singer and songwriter, best known by his stage name Lil' Dave Thompson.  He is best known for his tracks "She Didn't Say Goodbye" and "I Got the Blues".

name: Pyeng Threadgill

albums.name: Sweet Home: Pyeng Threadgill Sings Robert Johnson (2004)

description: Pyeng Dubra Threadgill (born November 14, 1977) is an American blues, jazz and soul blues singer, songwriter, and record producer.  Her father is the bandleader and composer, Henry Threadgill, and her mother is Christina Jones, a dancer and choreographer.  Threadgill has released three albums, beginning in 2004 with Sweet Home: Pyeng Threadgill Sings Robert Johnson.

name: Teeny Tucker
description: Regina B.  Higginbotham (born January 22, 1958) known professionally as Teeny Tucker is an American electric blues and new blues singer and songwriter.  She is the daughter of the late blues musician  Tommy Tucker.

name: Mike Wheeler
description: Mike Wheeler (born March 15, 1964) is an American Chicago blues guitarist, singer and songwriter. A veteran of the Chicago blues scene, Wheeler has played with numerous blues legends and leads his own band, blending traditional Chicago blues with contemporary sounds.

name: Albert White
description: Albert White (born June 15, 1942) is an American blues guitarist and singer. Known for his work in the soul blues tradition, White has been performing since the 1960s and is respected for his smooth vocal style and accomplished guitar work.

name: Sean Costello
description: Sean Costello (April 16, 1979 – April 15, 2008) was an American blues guitarist and singer. A prodigy who was performing with local bands in Atlanta by age 14, he was widely regarded as one of the most promising young blues musicians of his generation. Costello's playing blended traditional electric blues with soul, rock, and jazz influences. He released four acclaimed albums before his untimely death at age 28, just one day before his 29th birthday.

name: Lou Rawls

albums.name: When You Hear Lou, You've Heard It All (Philadelphia International, 1977)

description: Lou Rawls (1933-2006) was a renowned American baritone singer whose velvety smooth voice bridged gospel, blues, jazz, and soul. Beginning his career singing in church choirs in Chicago, he later moved to Los Angeles and became one of the most distinctive vocalists in soul and R&B, known for hits like 'You'll Never Find Another Love Like Mine' and 'Love Is a Hurtin' Thing'. Rawls won three Grammy Awards for Best Male R&B Vocal Performance and sold over 40 million records during his career, while also becoming known for his extensive charity work with the United Negro College Fund.

name: Ray Charles

albums.name: Modern Sounds in Country and Western Music (ABC-Paramount, 1962)

description: Ray Charles (1930-2004) was a revolutionary American singer, songwriter, and pianist who pioneered soul music by blending blues, jazz, R&B, and gospel. Blind since childhood, Charles overcame tremendous obstacles to become one of the most influential musicians of the 20th century, with groundbreaking hits like 'I've Got a Woman', 'Georgia on My Mind', and 'What'd I Say'. He broke racial barriers in the music industry and became one of the first black artists to gain creative control over his recordings, winning 17 Grammy Awards and earning induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame as a charter member. Frank Sinatra called him 'the only true genius in show business'.

name: Big Jack Johnson

albums.name: Daddy, When Is Mama Comin' Home? (1991)

description: Big Jack Johnson (July 30, 1940 – March 14, 2011) was an American electric blues musician from Lambert, Mississippi. A key figure in the Hill Country blues tradition, Johnson was known for his raw, electrified Delta blues sound and his work with the Jelly Roll Kings. He played guitar, mandolin, and vocals, and won a W.C. Handy Award in 2003 for Best Acoustic Blues Album. Johnson was also called 'The Oil Man' due to his work driving trucks for Shell Oil.

name: Booba Barnes
description: Roosevelt Melvin 'Booba' Barnes (September 25, 1936 – April 2, 1996) was an American Hill Country blues guitarist and vocalist from Longwood, Mississippi. Barnes started his career in 1960 with the Swinging Gold Coasters, later moved to Chicago, then returned to Mississippi in 1971. He opened the Playboy Club nightclub in 1985 and became a regional favorite. His 1990 debut album 'The Heartbroken Man' was hailed as an instant modern classic. Barnes died of lung cancer in 1996.

name: James "Super Chikan" Johnson
description: James 'Super Chikan' Johnson (born February 16, 1951) is an American Hill Country blues musician from Darling, Mississippi. The nephew of Big Jack Johnson, Super Chikan is a leading contemporary exponent of the North Mississippi Hill Country blues style. He began playing as a child on a diddley bow and bought his first guitar at age 13. Since his 1997 debut album, he has won multiple Blues Music Awards and is known for performing regularly at Morgan Freeman's Ground Zero blues club in Clarksdale. He also handcrafts artistic guitars from recycled parts.

name: John Cephas
description: John Cephas was a master of the Piedmont blues style, known for his fingerpicking guitar and warm vocals. Born in Washington D.C. but raised in Bowling Green, Virginia, he learned guitar from neighborhood musicians. He worked as a carpenter at the D.C. Armory until the late 1980s. In 1976, he met harmonica player Phil Wiggins, forming the legendary duo Cephas & Wiggins. They toured extensively as cultural ambassadors for the U.S. State Department, bringing Piedmont blues to audiences worldwide. Cephas received a National Heritage Fellowship in 1989, the nation's highest honor in folk and traditional arts.

name: Phil Wiggins
description: Phil Wiggins was a virtuoso harmonica player who, with guitarist John Cephas, formed one of the most celebrated acoustic blues duos of the modern era. Born and raised in Washington D.C., Wiggins mastered the Piedmont blues style, influenced by the great Sonny Terry. He met Cephas at the 1976 Smithsonian Folklife Festival, and they performed together for over three decades as Cephas & Wiggins. Wiggins was renowned for his rhythmic, driving harmonica style that perfectly complemented Cephas' fingerpicking guitar. He received a National Heritage Fellowship in 2017, recognizing his role in preserving and advancing the Piedmont blues tradition.
